name: projectile_sweep_kamikaze_friendly_exemption_0084c1d8
coverage: read only: 0084C1D8-0084C211, step 6 of 0084BF00's entity sweep. Not bound in any host.
original_abi: In-function. EBX = the sweep's hit flag from 0098B370; ESI = [ESP+44h] = the owner's +9D4h latched at 0084BF60; ECX = [ESP+78h] = the hit entity; [ESP+64h] = the projectile class descriptor.
evidence: Listing 0084C1D8-0084C211. The arm clears the hit (XOR BL,BL at 0084C211) only when all four hold: the owner's +CCh passed IsKindOf(0Fh) so [ESP+44h] is non-zero (0084C1E4 JZ), the sweep reported a hit (0084C1E8 JZ), the hit entity passes vtable[5Ch](0Fh) (0084C1FD JZ), classDesc[+8h] == 11h (0084C203 CMP / 0084C207 JNZ), and hitEntity[+9D4h] == owner[+9D4h] (0084C209 CMP / 0084C20F JNZ). Sub-type 11h is Kamikaze (include/bsp/projectile_kinds.hpp kProjectileSubTypeKamikaze); a torpedo is 0Ah. So this is a kamikaze exemption and NOT a general friendly-fire rule: the image lets a dropped torpedo hit a friendly aircraft. The sweep's own exclusion, EDI = owner->vtable[B0h]() at 0084C1B3-0084C1BF, is the shooter's collision root and covers one entity and its children (0098AEE4, 0098ACE3), not a squadron.
uncertainty: The four predicates and the constant are read from the listing. What the image does when two friendly aircraft are close enough for this to matter was not measured in the image; the packet only establishes that no arm on this path exempts a torpedo. Names are hypotheses.
